record.file_problem: The post is present in full. It refers to plots and audio examples that are not rendered in the supplied text, so their specific contents are unavailable.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures neuron responses using audio examples at different activation ranges, testing whether apparent polysemanticity depends on the range examined. This is a conceptual test of V7 using an audio model and qualitative listening rather than the claim's vision-model examples.
record.gate_note: The post reports that neurons 1 and 3 in the encoder's block.2.mlp.1 initially appeared to respond to one phoneme in maximally activating examples, but appeared polysemantic at other activation levels. Specific sounds and activation ranges are in plots/audio examples not rendered here. The encoder-attention, transcript-removal, and decoder language-model results do not measure the claim versions. References to polysemanticity in other work are not this study's results.
record.test_reason: It applies max-activating dataset examples to MLP neurons in an audio transformer (Whisper tiny), a setting not covered by the originals. It reports that neurons which look single-phoneme at maximum activation turn out polysemantic at other activation ranges, which bears directly on V7. The evidence is qualitative listening, not a scored measure, so this is a new-setting test (T3) rather than T2.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right but incomplete. The author's stated conclusions are that Whisper's encoder acoustic features are human-interpretable (with a method for listening to them), encoder attention is highly localized, and the decoder alone acts as a weak LM. The observation that some acoustic neurons are polysemantic, revealed by examining non-maximal activation ranges, is a subsection result and is not repeated in the conclusion.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses maximally activating dataset examples, as in the cited neuron-interpretation approach, and listens to examples across activation ranges. It applies this qualitatively to audio features rather than the cited vision-model examples.
record.method_sensitivity: The apparent interpretation of neurons 1 and 3 changes with the activation range examined: maximum-activation examples appeared single-phoneme, while varying levels revealed polysemantic behaviour.
record.problems: The activation-range evidence is qualitative, and the specific plots and audio examples are not rendered in the supplied text. The author notes that features were demonstrated using dataset examples rather than an optimization-based method, potentially biasing them toward the dataset. The reported polysemantic-neuron examination is limited to two neurons in one model.
record.rows_left_out: No other claim-relevant neuron results were stated separately. The table of phoneme interpretations for the first 50 neurons concerns feature interpretability but does not report polysemanticity or activation-range dependence.

untested.parts: Not tested: the study uses an audio model, not image classifiers.
Not tested: no prevalence of polysemantic MLP neurons in language models, and no layer comparison. Decoder neurons are only shown as semantically coherent.
Not tested: superposition or feature-count pressure as a cause.
Not tested: initialization, regularization or training noise as causes.
Not tested: no comparison of activation functions, architectures or regularization.
Not tested: no analysis of whether the mixed sounds share one feature.
Not tested: how explanation scoring affects the verdict. No numeric activation thresholds and no count of affected neurons are given.

record.verdict_notes: This is a LessWrong post from SERI MATS work and is not peer reviewed. The polysemanticity evidence rests on unrendered plots and audio. The 50-neuron table gives max-activation labels, some of which are grouped related phonemes (e.g. 'j/ch/sh'). It does not measure polysemanticity of unrelated inputs, so it was not made into rows.

versions.untested_parts: The study examines an audio model, not image classifiers or the stated vision-model examples.
It does not measure polysemanticity in language-model MLP neurons.
It does not test superposition or capacity pressure as a cause.
It does not test initialization, regularization, or training noise as causes.
It does not compare activation functions, architectures, or regularization, or measure whether polysemanticity can be reduced without performance loss.
It does not establish that mixed responses share a feature or are related offshoots of one job.
The study does not report numeric activation thresholds, a formal explanation-scoring method, or comparisons across models.
